events.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
events.summary:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.

Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

The UK would not have to follow the EU and apply tariffs on Chinese car imports under an Irish proposal that could prove another breakthrough for the prime minister, Andy Burnham, in his reset of relations with the bloc.

The proposal comes as the UK’s foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, told a parliamentary committee that there had been “a transformation in the EU view”.

Continue reading...

events.title: Leftwing coalition leader calls for rental revolution as Spain heads for snap election
events.summary:
Exclusive: Ada Colau hopes public anger over housing will transfer into support for her Broad Front coalition in Sunday’s vote

The leader of Spain’s leftwing Broad Front coalition has called for a drastic rethink of the country’s entire housing rental system, and described the eviction of an 87-year-old woman – the spark for nationwide protests that in turn triggered Sunday’s snap general election – as “the last straw” for desperate tenants.

“We’re not interested in small changes,” Ada Colau, the former Barcelona mayor, told the Guardian in an interview. “We want to reform the entire rental sector.”

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘They don’t believe in freedom’: Yemenis plan their escape as Houthis advance on Aden
events.summary:
With Iran’s proxy fighters encircling the temporary capital, residents and NGOs prepare to evacuate

Hussein fled his home six years ago after it fell under Houthi control, moving as far south as he could to the port city of Aden, where there was a measure of safety.

The Saudi-backed Yemeni government had made the city its temporary capital; the hundreds of kilometres between it and the Houthis were well fortified.

Continue reading...

events.title: Israel attempts to jail Palestinian student at Hebrew University without trial
events.summary:
Mahdi Tounsi appeared to have suffered maltreatment at hearing where he was not allowed to hear prosecution case against him

Palestinian student Mahdi Tounsi appeared in a closed-door court hearing in Jerusalem, as academics and activists warned that Israel’s attempt to jail him without trial marked a serious escalation in attacks on Palestinian rights.

Yael Berda, a lawyer and sociology professor at Hebrew University, who has taught Tounsi for four years, came to court to call for his release.

Continue reading...

events.title: Gaza issues meningitis epidemic alert after steep rise in cases
events.summary:
Health ministry records 272 new infections in October, more than eight times the normal monthly rate

Gaza’s health ministry has issued an epidemic alert after a sharp rise in meningitis infections, with more than 270 new cases reported in October.

Dr Nidal Ghoneim, a senior official at the ministry, said the spread of the disease posed a threat to the lives of hundreds of thousands of people, including children.

Continue reading...

events.title: Iranian singer and four others receive lashes after performance without hijab
events.summary:
Western governments and rights groups have criticised flogging as torture and a violation of international law

An Iranian singer and four members of her production team ⁠have each received 74 lashes after being sentenced for “offending public decency by producing and ⁠publishing obscene and ⁠immoral ​content online”, an Iranian news website said on Monday.

Parastoo Ahmadi and the four ⁠others were also handed two-year bans on artistic and musical activities and travel, the Emtedad website ⁠quoted lawyer Mostafa Nili as saying.

Continue reading...

events.title: Israel seeks to jail Palestinian student activist without trial after dorm arrest
events.summary:
Mahdi Tounsi appeared with visible bruising after being interrogated by police on his association with Israeli-Palestinian organisations

Israeli professors, students and rights activists are calling for the immediate release of Mahdi Tounsi, a sociology student at Jerusalem’s Hebrew University who has been held without charge for more than two weeks after he was seized from his dorm room.

The detention comes amid a racist campaign of delegitimisation against Palestinian citizens of Israel, whose votes were critical to stripping Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition of its majority in elections last month.

Continue reading...

events.title: World Chess Championship 2026 Game 1: Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov play to 38-move draw – as it happened
events.summary:
• Sindarov and Gukesh play to 38-move draw in Game 1

  • Explainer: all your pre-match questions, answered

  • Sindarov interview: ‘I can’t play games just for fun’

  • Play through 22 famous world championship games

The players have shaken hands and we’re off! We have a Berlin defense of the Ruy Lopez (1 e4 e5 2 Nf3 Nc6 3 Bb5 Nf6), one of the most thoroughly analyzed openings in modern chess.

The Berlin famously helped Vladimir Kramnik dethrone Garry Kasparov in their 2000 world title match in London and has been a staple of elite chess ever since, earning a reputation as one of black’s most reliable weapons against 1 e4.

Continue reading...

events.title: Leader of India’s Cockroach movement says he was stopped from boarding flight to UK
events.summary:
Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests.

Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May. Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.

Continue reading...

events.title: After 80 years in Oxford, Naga ancestors are finally going home
events.summary:
A campaign securing the landmark return to India of ancestral remains taken during British colonial rule has opened a wider conversation about restitution

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

The lacerating legacy of colonialism survives in many spaces, particularly in museum collections and private holdings across the western world. And it’s not just limited to inanimate artefacts or cultural objects.

For almost 80 years, human remains were displayed on crowded glass shelves at Pitt Rivers Museum at Oxford University, one of the world’s most celebrated institutions.

Continue reading...

events.title: Myanmar has been found guilty of genocide. Should Israel be worried? – podcast
events.summary:
The international court of justice has for the first time ruled that a state has committed genocide. Yasmin Ullah explains what it means for the Rohingya people, while Kaamil Ahmed lays out how the case unfolded

For seven years, Yasmin Ullah had been part of the delegation arguing that Myanmar had committed genocide – one of the gravest human rights crimes – against Rohingya Muslims.

The genocide has directly affected Yasmin and her family. Last week she was in court to hear the international court of justice’s landmark verdict against Myanmar. “I was really kind of pinching myself. It felt like we were all able to breathe again,” she tells Annie Kelly.

Continue reading...

events.title: Indian opposition party’s youth wing warns of more Meta protests after police clashes
events.summary:
Members of Congress party clashed with police outside tech company’s offices on Friday

The youth wing of India’s main opposition Congress party warned of more protests against Meta’s removal of some of its members’ ⁠accounts, ⁠a day after clashing with ​police outside the tech firm’s locals offices.

In Hyderabad on Friday, protesters ‌carrying placards and chanted slogans as they stormed into ‌the building that houses Meta’s offices, smashing plants to the ground and clashing with police, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress’s X account.

Continue reading...

events.title: Energy bills in Great Britain to rise 26% in January, lifting annual bills over £2,000
events.summary:
Ofgem’s price cap will increase for third quarter in a row after rise in wholesale cost of gas

Millions of British households will face annual energy bills of more than £2,000 a year for the first time since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, as the cap on energy bills climbs for a third straight quarter.

Gas and electricity prices will rise by 26% from January under the government’s new price cap after an increase in wholesale prices not experienced since the first winter after the invasion.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘Nature’s Ozempic’: oat sales soar as shoppers seek out foods that mimic effect of GLP-1s
events.summary:
Porridge emerges as trend’s poster child with consumers looking to foods that help them feel full for longer, says Waitrose

Sales of filling foods such as porridge oats that mimic the effect of taking weight-loss medication are booming on the back of social media hype billing them as “nature’s Ozempic” or “oatzempic”.

Sales of Waitrose Scottish Oats are up 124% this year, according to the retailer’s annual food and drink report, which dissects the biggest trends sweeping the grocery aisles. A poll conducted for the report revealed that 64% of shoppers are “actively choosing to eat foods like oats that keep us feeling fuller for longer”.

Continue reading...

events.title: China-linked battery projects could receive UK funding despite security warnings
events.summary:
China-made lithium-ion batteries, which are relatively low-cost, dominate Ofgem project shortlist

A string of battery projects linked to China are expected to be granted UK state subsidies despite deepening fears over the risk of foreign interference they could pose to Europe’s energy systems.

Ofgem, Great Britain’s energy regulator, published a provisional shortlist for a new “long duration” energy storage scheme in June. The list was dominated by projects relying on lithium-ion batteries, which are typically manufactured in China and operated with Chinese software.

Continue reading...

events.title: Middle-aged women in England least likely to successfully quit smoking, study finds
events.summary:
Of nearly 8,000 women who tried to stop, only 18% of those aged 45 to 60 managed to give up

Middle-aged women in England are the least likely to successfully give up smoking, according to research.

Smoking is the leading cause of preventable death and illness in the UK. While overall smoking rates in England have declined in recent decades, rates in some regions have increased. About 6.75 million people smoke in England, of whom around 14% are women aged 45-60.

Continue reading...

events.title: Latest review of Met police culture finds little has changed since last one
events.summary:
Failure to implement previous reports means institutional racism, misogyny and homophobia still present in force

  • Metropolitan police still institutionally racist and misogynist, says report

From the Stephen Lawrence inquiry in 1999 to Louise Casey’s landmark review in 2023, successive reports on the Metropolitan police have arrived at the same damning conclusion: Britain’s largest police force is institutionally racist.

It will, therefore, come as little surprise that three years after Casey’s report, an independent review led by Gillian Fairfield has found that institutional racism, misogyny and homophobia persist within the force.

Continue reading...

events.title: Trump reportedly says he is open to pardoning Jensen Huang ahead of CEO’s planned Senate committee testimony – as it happened
events.summary:
This live blog is now closed.

  • Schumer accuses Huang of violating US export control laws amid shipments of chips to China

Earlier we mentioned Donald Trump is participating in a Medal of Freedom ceremony in the Oval Office at 11am ET. He will be awarding the nation’s highest civilian honor to former New York mayor and Trump’s onetime personal lawyer Rudy Giuliani.

Trump said last year he would award the medal to Giuliani, two days after his longtime political ally was seriously injured in a car crash.

events.title: Al Gore buys local, family-owned newspaper in central Tennessee
events.summary:
Former vice-president, who started his career as a journalist, purchases Carthage Courier in Smith county

Al Gore, who started his career as a journalist, is returning to the industry as a newspaper owner in his Tennessee town.

The Lake family, which has operated the Carthage Courier for five decades, said Tuesday it will sell the paper to the former vice-president in the coming weeks. The weekly paper serves Smith county in central Tennessee, which has roughly 20,000 residents and sits about 55 miles (88km) east of Nashville.

Continue reading...

events.title: Rescue crews search for six people after plane crash off Mississippi coast
events.summary:
US Coast Guard said crews had so far found the cabin of the plane, a life raft and three life jackets

Rescue crews were searching for six people on board a small plane that crashed Tuesday afternoon off the coast of Mississippi.

Crews have so far found three life jackets, a life raft and the cabin of the plane. The plane’s cabin was floating on the water, Juan Ros, a US Coast Guard spokesperson, said.

Continue reading...

events.title: One lame duck and two turkeys as Trump plays the hits at Thanksgiving ceremony
events.summary:
Levity was in short supply as president, reeling from midterms rout, talked up his achievements – and fixated on White House vanity project

For some, it was his pardoning of the January 6 rioters or the deployment of masked ICE agents. For others, it was Elon Musk’s chainsaw or the demolition of the White House East Wing.

Donald Trump’s second term as US president has been full of moments when people exclaim: this is the last straw! But on Tuesday even he went too far.

Continue reading...

events.title: US army to detonate 68 barrels of toxic lead in Iowa on day before Thanksgiving
events.summary:
Residents warned to stay indoors amid conflicting information about how far the dust plume could travel

The US Army is set to detonate 68 barrels – five tons – of lead azide at an ammunition plant in rural Iowa on Wednesday morning, after delays and conflicting information about how far the toxic lead dust plume could travel after the explosion.

That controlled blast has been scheduled for 10am ET on Wednesday, the day before the Thanksgiving holiday.

events.title: Who really owns the Albanian land Jared Kushner wants to turn into a 5-star resort?
events.summary: Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama has vowed that Kushner's resort project will go ahead as planned. But an ongoing investigation by Albania's state prosecutor into forged land titles could halt the project.

events.title: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia. And, Rep. Gomez resigns amid alleged sexual misconduct
events.summary: President Trump took credit for negotiating Jensen Huang's return as CEO of Nvidia. And, Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., says his resignation will be effective Dec. 1.

events.title: The human cost of the electric vehicle boom is at the center of a lawsuit in Congo
events.summary: A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them.

events.title: Meet Colombia's fuzzy 'water guardians'
events.summary: High in the Colombian Andes, a growing number of volunteers are racing to save an unusual plant that helps supply water to millions — one tiny seedling at a time.

events.title: Fighting between Russia and Ukraine has expanded geographically, drawing concerns
events.summary: In recent days, Ukraine has sunk a Russian warship docked in port in Libya, and Russian missiles have landed in Poland. The Kremlin has not commented on the missiles.

events.title: Russian incursions into NATO territory are increasing
events.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte is seeking to reassure the alliance's eastern European members after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland on Friday.

events.title: Democrats win House by largest margin in 50 years. And, COP31 ends with no deal
events.summary: Democrats have currently flipped 47 House seats and could flip 49 total. And, climate change talks at COP31 ran two days longer than expected, becoming the longest conference in the summit's history.

events.title: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
events.summary: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault.

events.summary: The war between Russia and Ukraine once again creeps onto European territory – from attacks on ships to missiles in Poland and fresh allegations of Russian operations inside Denmark.

events.summary: Every three days in Germany, a man kills his wife or ex-partner. Every 10 minutes, the police record a sexual offense against a woman. "A shocking finding," according to Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig.

events.title: India news: US prepares new tariffs after trade probe
events.summary: The United States is reportedly readying fresh tariffs on India and 15 other economies under a trade probe. Also, a woman was allegedly gangraped by her colleagues in the national capital. Follow live.

events.title: Libya: 2 dead after Ukrainian attack on Russian warship in Benghazi
events.summary: The head of the eastern administration in Libya has confirmed that two Libyan soldiers succumbed to their injuries. Ukraine's foreign minister defended the attack as an effort to counter Russian aggression.

events.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 to Tiangong station
events.summary: A new Chinese crew is on its way to the Tiangong station after a launch that China called a complete success. This includes a Pakistani pilot, who is making a brief visit.

events.title: US jury convicts Huawei of violating sanctions, stealing trade secrets
events.summary: Huawei was found guilty of 10 out of 12 charges levelled against it. The company said it plans to appeal the verdict.

events.title: Scientists discover quasar formed 630 million years after the Big Bang
events.summary: Scientists are seeing the quasar as it was 13.1 billion years ago — when the universe was less than 5% of its current age.

events.title: European court finds states can turn back migrants in some cases
events.summary: Europe's top human rights court ruled that member states can turn back migrants unless they've been identified as people who were at risk of suffering.

events.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy and Hungary's Magyar meet amid thaw in ties
events.summary: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar has arrived in Ukraine for meetings with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and ethnic Hungarians. Both leaders say they want better relations after a change of leadership in Budapest.

events.title: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
events.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

events.title: HIV infections could rise amid aid cuts, UN warns
events.summary: The impact of United States government funding cuts has been dramatic for many HIV programs, UNAIDS warned. The agency expects that 2027 data to show an increase in new infections after being on the cusp of ending AIDS.

events.title: Pope Francis diaries recount spiritual crisis, him seeing the 'Devil'
events.summary: Extracts of the late Pope Francis' diaries have been published, the first release of its kind since the 1960s. They discuss his struggles with his role in the Vatican and visions of the devil and the gates of hell.

events.title: EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?
events.summary: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process — often for reasons of domestic politics. DW takes a look at some cases and examines what's behind them.

events.title: CAS reinstates Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions
events.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has reinstated Senegal as 2025 AFCON champions, overturning a CAF decision that stripped them of the title. Morocco, previously declared winners, are confirmed runners-up.

events.title: Why Iran's medicine supply chain is failing
events.summary: Pharmacies in Iran are closing, hospital deliveries have stalled and patients are rationing doses or turning to black markets.

events.title: Colombia: Car bomb attack injures at least 23
events.summary: The explosion in Villavicencio coincides with the tenth anniversary of a peace accord with FARC guerrillas, casting doubt on Colombia's peace process.

events.title: Germany's Wadephul 'shocked' by Trump's Nvidia intervention
events.summary: The German foreign minister has criticized Donald Trump's interference in the chip-maker's economic activities. Jensen Huang was brought back after stepping down as Nvidia CEO amid multiple scandals.

events.title: Land mine deaths reach five-year high, watchdog says
events.summary: Myanmar reported the highest annual land mine casualty toll, followed by Syria and Afghanistan, ICBL report says. Since 1999, nearly 50 thousand people were killed by land mines.

events.title: Is North Korea holding back on sending Russia more troops?
events.summary: A North Korean troop buildup Ukraine warned about months ago has yet to materialize, even as strategic cooperation continues. Analysts say Pyongyang is balancing its ties with Moscow and Beijing.

events.title: Five women killed every hour by family members or partners — UN report
events.summary: On average, 129 women or girls were killed every day in 2025 by someone in their close social circle, UN data showed.

events.title: Bombed factories, billion-dollar opportunity: Why German companies are staying in Ukraine
events.summary: German companies remain committed to Ukraine despite million-dollar losses, an unreliable energy supply and a shortage of skilled workers. They are betting on new markets and long-term growth.

events.title: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble
events.summary: From Nvidia to Coreweave, AI and tech stocks have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see plenty of room to run, while others are trying to diversify — and finding it harder than expected.

events.title: German directors' doc on stolen film wins International Emmy Award
events.summary: Two German film students confronted the American who won festival prizes with their animated movie. "The Talented Mr. F," their documentary on their fight against plagiarism, is now in the spotlight.

events.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
events.summary: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.

events.title: Weapons, war and wavering trust: Germans want to see more restraint in foreign policy
events.summary: According to a study by the Körber Foundation, a growing number of Germans now oppose providing military aid to Ukraine. The majority also believes that Germany should take a neutral position between the US and China.

events.title: US and UK to host Women's World Cups in 2031 and 2035
events.summary: FIFA has confirmed the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host the 2031 Women's World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams. The UK will stage the 2035 edition, its first World Cup since 1966.

events.title: Gukesh to defend chess crown against rising star Sindarov
events.summary: As the World Chess championship gets underway, it's no coincidence that the titleholder, Gukesh Dommaraju, and his challenger, Jakhovir Sindarov, are both from Asia.

events.title: Nvidia reinstates former CEO Jensen Huang despite China espionage scandal
events.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring back the disgraced CEO, who resigned this month amid news of his affairs. He's suspected of having had a relationship with a Chinese intelligence asset.

events.title: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate
events.summary: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.

events.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
events.summary: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

events.title: COP deadlock prompts calls for a reset of climate diplomacy
events.summary: COP31 has been branded a failure after countries couldn't reach a final agreement, divided over a reference to "fossil fuels." But was the decision to walk away from a watered-down text actually a show of strength?

events.title: German police respond to multiple school bomb threats
events.summary: Police in Germany are responding to bomb threats against a series of schools, but say that at present they don't believe them to be credible. Danish authorities are reporting a similar series of apparent hoaxes.

events.title: 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract
events.summary: For decades, Germans have known Hollywood's biggest stars through the same familiar voices. Now an AI clause in Netflix contracts is splitting the industry over whether it protects performers or exposes them.

events.title: Budget cuts threaten Germany's fight against antisemitism and racism
events.summary: Numerous grassroots initiatives in Germany are facing funding cuts. Affected organizations are sounding the alarm, pointing to growing challenges posed by far-right extremism.

events.title: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect
events.summary: A new project and exhibition, "The Night Watch Lives," lifts the veil on the hidden world of microbes covering one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.

events.title: Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?
events.summary: Germany plans to pay €10 a month into investment accounts for children to encourage long-term retirement saving. Economists say the measure may help build wealth but won't solve the country's pension funding challenge.

events.title: Germany news: Metalworkers go on strike as pay dispute heats up
events.summary: Germany's biggest union is calling for more strikes over heated pay disputes with car makers like Mercedes and shipyards among the companies impacted. Meanwhile, a Berlin hospital fire leaves many injured.

events.title: Rule-breaking is contagious — and good examples barely help
events.summary: Seeing someone break a rule makes people more likely to break it too, a new study finds, especially when the rule-breaker is on their side politically. Watching others behave well barely made a difference.

events.title: COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use
events.summary: After two weeks of tough talks, the COP31 climate summit has closed without a consensus on how to quit fossil fuels or fund countries struggling to adapt to a hotter world.

events.title: Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029
events.summary: "The Goodforces" wants to see a swing to the left in the 2029 German elections. The agency counts New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Bernie Sanders among its inspirations. Could it transform the political landscape?

events.title: Germany news: IG Metall union calls for new 24-hour strike
events.summary: Germany's biggest single union, IG Metall, is calling on car and shipyard workers to strike amid a pay row. Meanwhile, Germany's president is setting off on an Africa trip. DW has more.

events.title: Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
events.summary: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.

events.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
events.summary: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.

events.title: EU takes aim at tech giants in tax proposal
events.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

events.title: Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
events.summary: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

events.title: Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad
events.summary: Harassment, persecution, surveillance: Across much of the world, people of faith are facing growing pressure. A new German government report is unusually direct in criticizing China in particular.

events.title: Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
events.summary: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.

events.title: COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading
events.summary: Attacks on climate science and disinformation risk delaying key measures at COP31 in Antalya. As the UN climate talks draw to a close, how will that affect efforts to come to an agreement?

events.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
events.summary: The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

events.title: Better educated than ever — yet Germany's Gen Z is being shut out of its own future
events.summary: Never before have young people around the world been so well-educated while facing so many economic challenges. Young Germans are asking: Will I be better off than my parents?

events.title: Can German auto manufacturing recover after Mercedes and VW cuts?
events.summary: German automakers are pulling back on investments at home, sparking fresh anxiety about the auto sector's future. Some industry watchers think there is still a narrow window to stem the decline. But how?

events.title: Measles in America: Here's a constructive approach to beating the disease, based on Brazil's experience
events.summary: The US is now officially a measles contagion zone. By mid-2026, there were more infections than in all of the previous year. But the country could beat measles again, just like Brazil did two years ago.

events.title: Germany face Belgium in Nations League quarterfinals — Klopp plays down favorites tag
events.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is looking to "carry positive momentum forward" as his team draw neighboring Belgium in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League.

events.title: EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
events.summary: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.

events.title: FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?

events.title: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs, citing ongoing losses — reports

events.title: Have we missed our chance to stop climate change?
events.summary: From record-breaking heat to devastating floods and wildfires, the warning signs are everywhere. Can rising temperatures still be brought under control?

events.title: Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?

events.title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
events.summary: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.

events.title: Anthropic trading tests investors' appetite for AI
events.summary: Anthropic was valued at $2 trillion after shares started trading on the Nasdaq following a record $81 billion IPO. Its performance will put investor confidence in AI to the test.

events.title: Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend
events.summary: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev is facing a new lawsuit related to a domestic abuse trial. The lawyer for his ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, told DW what the allegations are against the German player.

events.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
events.summary: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

events.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
events.summary: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

events.title: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure
events.summary: As Donald Trump seeks to tighten economic pressure on Iran, China remains its biggest oil customer and Russia a key partner. But both powers are balancing support for Tehran against broader interests with Washington.

events.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
events.summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

events.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
events.summary: Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.

events.title: 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine
events.summary: The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.

events.title: How a green economy could help reverse climate change
events.summary: Green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?

events.title: Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
events.summary: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

events.title: Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
events.summary: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.

events.title: Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
events.summary: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

events.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
events.summary: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.

events.title: Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
events.summary: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

events.title: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future
events.summary: Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters offers hope.

events.title: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?
events.summary: The US says a record €3 billion financing package for Airbus may conflict with a transatlantic aircraft-subsidy truce. EU officials insist the funding complies with market-based rules.

events.title: Germany news: Plans for Rwanda migrant hub come under fire
events.summary: Human rights groups have slammed plans by Germany and four other EU states to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. In other news, business start-ups in Germany are on track to reach the highest level since 2015.

events.title: France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
events.summary: Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.

events.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth
events.summary: When just saying 'hello' takes a two-day round trip, you're a light-day, or 26 billion kilometers, from Earth. Only one human-made object has ever traveled that far — and its journey into interstellar space continues.

events.title: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades
events.summary: In 1962, a martini-drinking womanizer saved the world for the first time in "Dr. No." As Robert Pattinson takes on the role of 007, here's how the films evolved.

events.title: The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?
events.summary: The Alternative for Germany party (AfD) has become a focal point for the far right. Many of its members and staff have ties to ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations.

events.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels
events.summary: The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.

events.title: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms
events.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

events.title: Germany news: Merz, Söder aim to revisit electricity tax cut
events.summary: The Christian Democrats are in Munich, pushing to revive some tax relief that didn't make it into the budget after talks last week. And Manuela Schwesig faces a vote on a new term as regional leader. Follow DW.

events.title: Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?
events.summary: In April, about 60 countries held an unprecedented meeting in Colombia to work out a plan to slowly quit oil, coal and gas. How influential is this coalition at the COP31 climate summit?

events.title: AI in classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'
events.summary: Research suggests that students who aren't careful about how they use ChatGPT and other AI tools risk poorer academic outcomes. It's a huge challenge for teachers.

events.title: German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?
events.summary: The German economy is growing again, albeit slightly. However, economists warn that without reforms, higher productivity and solid public finances, a loss of prosperity and growing debt threaten future generations.

events.title: Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
events.summary: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

events.title: Germany news: Germany holds national day of remembrance
events.summary: Events were held for "Volkstrauertag," a day commemorating victims of war and oppression. Meanwhile, experts said the country is headed for a budget crisis.

events.title: How AI is likely to change Germany's job market
events.summary: The scale of the economic disruption caused by AI has led even conservative politicians to talk about universal basic income. But economists aren't convinced, and campaigners think we need to ask deeper questions.

events.title: Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt
events.summary: The 2027 federal budget proposal has finally been hammered out and is set for a vote in parliament. What are the government's policy priorities in defense, infrastructure, the economy and social spending?

events.title: Werner Holzer Prize awarded to Katja Gloger and DW's Jaafar Abdul Karim
events.summary: DW journalist Jaafar Abdul Karim and Russia correspondent Katja Gloger have been awarded the prestigious Werner Holzer Prize for international journalism.

events.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
events.summary: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

events.title: Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany
events.summary: His life is a reflection of contemporary German history, addressed via his songs and sharp wit. At 90, he's as feisty as ever.

events.title: Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics
events.summary: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

events.title: Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
events.summary: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

events.title: The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
events.summary: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

events.title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
events.summary: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

events.title: Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany
events.summary: Two weeks after the CAS ordered ice hockey's governing body to reintegrate Russia into international play, a solution remains elusive. Now Russia has threatened to take legal action against two tournament hosts.

events.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
events.summary: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has said midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.

events.title: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?
events.summary: The TFFF rainforest fund aims to make forest conservation more profitable than deforestation. But a lack of money may prevent it from getting off the ground.

events.title: Iranian activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi shares her story in memoir
events.summary: Written and smuggled out of prison, the 2023 Nobel Prize laureate's memoir reveals the cost of defying Iran's regime and fighting for freedom.

events.title: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO
events.summary: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO over extramarital affairs. DW examines how losing its figurehead will affect the firm and the US-China AI race.

events.title: What are fossil fuels?
events.summary: They are in our shampoo bottles, power our cars and heat our homes. But what actually are fossil fuels, and why do they matter?

events.title: Intelligent women get less help at work, study finds
events.summary: Women who scored high on intelligence tests were seen as more hostile by their teammates and got less help, a new study finds. High-scoring men faced no such penalty. Research explains why.

events.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
events.summary: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

events.title: Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?
events.summary: World leaders warn that geopolitical divisions are distracting from the climate crisis as negotiations focus on clean energy and financing, while Iran calls for compensation for war-related environmental damage.

events.title: DW Science explainer on the default mode network: what your brain does when you aren't focusing on anything, and why it's important.
events.summary: Doing nothing might be the ultimate brain hack. When you're bored, the brain goes into default mode network. It's not only healthy for you, but it may also shape the very essence of your identity.

events.title: Germany slips in climate protection rankings as other countries make gains
events.summary: Record renewable energy growth is driving climate progress in some countries, but Germany and many major emitters are falling behind.

events.title: Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?
events.summary: Hitler once called Eastern Europe "Germany's India." A new exhibition examines the links between colonialism and Nazism, and the bitter debate over where comparisons illuminate history and where they fall short.

events.title: Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future
events.summary: Manuel Neuer's latest injury gives Jonas Urbig a run of games in Bayern's goal. Marc-André ter Stegen remains Germany’s No. 1, but Urbig now has a chance to strengthen his case for the future.

events.title: Megaspeed and the battle to go high-end Nvidia chips into China
events.summary: Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy has shone a light on Megaspeed, the company she worked for. It is under investigation in the US for smuggling Nvidia chips into China, which it denies.

events.title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion
events.summary: Felix Nmecha's "Crowns down" celebration has drawn criticism from a Borussia Dortmund fan club, reopening debate over faith, inclusion and religious messaging in football.

events.title: Why electrification is the climate game changer we need
events.summary: From EVs and electric buses on the road, heat pumps warming homes and solar panels powering appliances, the shift to electrifying tech is already in full swing. But what exactly does "electrification" mean?

events.title: Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?
events.summary: The heat is on Australia as chief negotiator at the COP31 UN climate conference to forge a path away from coal and gas, and to protect Pacific neighbors facing rising sea levels.

events.title: Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health
events.summary: More than 2 billion people worldwide suffer from nutrient deficiencies, most of them in the Global South. The health consequences can be devastating.

events.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
events.summary: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the trend.

events.title: Norway's ice hockey team says Russia replacing it at World Juniors
events.summary: The wrangling over Russia's return to international ice hockey continues, with Norway saying it has been kicked out of the next major tournament to accommodate Russia. Switzerland has joined a "boycott."

events.title: 37 years after fall of Berlin Wall: How divided are Germans?
events.summary: Three artists share their thoughts on the reunification of East and West Germany. How do they perceive a shared "we" and what gives them cause for optimism?

events.title: Why Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy matters for AI race
events.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has apologized for an affair with a woman the US believes was spying for China. The story could have profound implications for the world's most valuable company and the global AI race.

events.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
events.summary: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

events.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
events.summary: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

events.title: Germany hopes to host world ice hockey championship — without Russia
events.summary: International protests continue after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey. Germany is seeking a solution that will allow the country to host next year's world championship.

events.title: Amid protests, France's rising debt costs threaten stability
events.summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

events.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
events.summary: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

events.title: Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response
events.summary: A record heat wave. Five years of drought. A nation under pressure. Germany is running its biggest joint crisis exercise to date to test how authorities would cope with an escalating climate emergency.

events.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
events.summary: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

events.title: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival
events.summary: Evidence suggests exercise can keep more cancer patients alive. But what does "living longer" actually mean, and who does it apply to?

events.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
events.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets.

events.title: Russia is back in world sport, but who is drug testing its athletes?
events.summary: DW has found that three-quarters of Russia's weightlifting team had no independent out-of-competition testing before this year's world championships, despite the country's doping history.

events.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces retirement from international football
events.summary: The announcement by the footballing legend comes just weeks after a public spat with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over playing time.

events.title: What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump
events.summary: From high oil prices and data centers to tariffs and mounting debt, economic concerns played a key role in the crushing defeat of President Donald Trump's Republicans. So can the Democrats now make a difference?

events.title: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat
events.summary: The occupied West Bank is not an obvious breeding ground for sporting success. But Mariam Bsharat, 17, has beaten the odds to become a karate world champion and is making a new life in Germany.

events.title: Harry Potter films turns 25 ahead of new TV series' release
events.summary: In 2001, "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" hit cinemas and took the world by storm. Today, anticipation for the new series is high, but its creator, J.K. Rowling, remains a controversial figure.

events.title: Leading ice hockey nations, sponsors oppose Russia's return
events.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

events.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
events.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

events.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
events.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

events.title: Could AI give NFTs a second chance?
events.summary: NFTs have plunged in value since their pandemic height in 2021. In some cases, they are worth 99% less than they were paid for. Yet tokenization of real-world assets and AI means the curios may yet have a future.

events.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
events.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

events.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
events.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

events.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
events.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

events.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
events.summary: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

events.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
events.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

events.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
events.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

events.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
events.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

events.title: 🔴 Colombia president says all hostages freed, one assailant killed after supermarket hostage siege
2025 AFCON: CAS gives title to Senegal as Morocco vows to challenge verdict
events.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has handed down its ruling: Senegal is officially the 2025 AFCON champion. The Moroccan Football Federation has announced that it will challenge the verdict, citing irregularities in the proceedings.

events.title: Amnesty calls for ICC genocide probe over Israel's impact on births in Gaza
events.summary: Amnesty International on Wednesday urged the International Criminal Court to investigate whether Israeli officials committed genocide in Gaza, citing measures it says have prevented births and severely harmed women's reproductive health. The rights group said it had serious concerns that these effects were intentional, while acknowledging it could not reach a definitive conclusion.

events.title: Live: Two Libyan soldiers killed in Ukrainian attack on Russian vessels in Benghazi
events.summary: Two Libyan soldiers have died from injuries sustained in an attack, claimed by Ukraine, on Russian ships near Benghazi, a senior figure in the administration in eastern Libya said late on Tuesday. Members of the European Parliament will convene in Strasbourg on Wednesday to discuss "Europe’s role and capacity to protect the international order and secure a just and lasting peace for Ukraine". Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

events.title: Ukraine seeks €115 billion in foreign aid for 2027, Zelensky says
events.summary: Ukraine will need €115 billion in external financing next year to sustain its economy and war effort against Russia, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, adding that Kyiv had secured commitments for about €90 billion from the European Union.

events.title: New York jury convicts Huawei of stealing trade secrets
events.summary: A New York jury on Tuesday found Chinese telecom giant Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offences, but acquitted it of a racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. The verdict followed a three-month trial in New York in a case that adds to longstanding US efforts to curb Huawei's operations over alleged threats to national security.

events.title: Champions League: Real Madrid thrash PSV 5-1 in comeback win as Manchester City held by Napoli
events.summary: Real Madrid extended their winning run to 10 games in all competitions on Tuesday, overturning an early deficit to rout PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League, with Jude Bellingham scoring a spectacular goal and Kylian Mbappé netting twice. Manchester City, meanwhile, twice came from behind to draw 2-2 with Napoli, while Arsenal were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund.

events.title: Tech executives' investment in Trump 'clearly paying off' as Huang reinstated at Nvidia
events.summary: Nvidia shares fell on Tuesday as the historic rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as CEO quickly lost steam, with investors refocusing ​on the political ‌and governance risks surrounding his reinstatement. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, The Hill Senior Technology Reporter Miranda Nazzaro says that the reinstatement of Jensen Huang at Nvidia represents "the culmination of a two-year push of tech executives to get closer to President Trump and their investment in the President is clearly paying off".

events.title: Tech executives' investment in Trump 'clearly paying off' as Huang reinstated at Nvidia
events.summary: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, The Hill Senior Technology Reporter Miranda Nazzaro says that the reinstatement of Jensen Huang at Nvidia represents "the culmination of a two-year push of tech executives to get closer to President Trump and their investment in the President is clearly paying off".

events.title: 'Quid pro quo’: Nvidia too big to fail or ‘too close to personal interest of people around Trump’?
events.summary: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of the Institute of Digital Sovereignty and Senior Lecturer in Internet Governance at Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University. What does Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia mean for Trump, Lutnick, the US, the AI industry and China? Describing Huang as “the global banker of the AI industry”, Benhamou explains: “He is the visionary, he is the banker. He's not only the chip maker.” He also warns of the repercussions of Donald Trump's decision to reinstate the Nvidia CEO, with congressional and judicial scrutiny looming. “It's far from over. It's just the beginning.”

events.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback sends AI videos into overdrive
events.summary: Just 11 days after resigning as Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang’s return has unleashed a fresh wave of AI-generated videos. But the internet has changed its tune: while last week’s memes mocked Huang, many now celebrate his comeback. One viral video purportedly showing him dancing is actually AI-manipulated footage of a basketball coach from 2016. From humiliation to hero worship, the technology Nvidia helped popularise is rewriting the narrative surrounding its own CEO, as Vedika Bahl explains.

events.title: Did Nvidia knowingly send chips to China 'cutout'? Was there ‘pay-to-play’ involving Trump, Lutnick?
events.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Andrew Weissmann, Professor of Practice at NYU School of Law and a former federal prosecutor known for leading major Department of Justice (DOJ) and FBI investigations. “Why were they treating Nvidia so favorably? Professor Weissmann joins us to discuss the legal and ethical questions surrounding the Trump administration's dealings with the chipmaker. He examines allegations of personal financial gain, the implications for US national security, the limits of presidential immunity and what he describes as an “unholy alliance of tech bros, of Wall Street, and of politicians."

events.title: Senegal reinstated as AFCON 2025 winners
events.summary: In tonight's edition, Senegal were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners after the sport's highest court upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title.

events.title: UN slams Iran after it flogs singer for performing without veil
events.summary: The United Nations condemned as "abhorrent" the flogging of Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her production team, urging Tehran to abolish the practice. The five received 74 lashes each on Monday following a performance viewed millions of times on YouTube, local media reported, citing Ahmadi's lawyer.

events.title: Russian nuclear satellites plan 'foolhardy', expert says
events.summary: NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin, Dafydd Townley, Senior Teaching Fellow in International Security at the University of Portsmouth, says that the alleged plan would be "foolhardy because the impact would be indiscriminate, they wouldn't be able to choose only Western or non-Russian satellites".

events.title: The Bukele method: will Salvadoran leader's strong-arm tactics work for Haiti?
events.summary: Haitians are hailing the Bukele method. Citizens of the Americas’ poorest nation cheering the Salvadoran president’s ’shoot first, ask questions later’ method of dealing with the gangs that have overrun their country the past six years. Can the police force deployed actually restore law and order? We’ll ask about the latest in a decades-long list of efforts by the international community to support Haiti.

events.title: Senegal AFCON ruling 'good in the books of sports law', expert says
events.summary: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin, sports presenter and journalist Thando Sibiya explains that the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport to reinstate Senegal as ⁠winner of ​the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations "from a jurisprudence perspective or creating precedent, it is going to be good in the books of sports law, because if every single decision of a referee is taken to a court of law all the time, it really tampers with the quality, governance and legitimacy of the game".

events.title: Senegal regain AFCON title on appeal at Morocco's expense
events.summary: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. CAS said in a statement it had "upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF)" by a "unanimous decision". FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

events.title: Car bomb destroys buildings in central Colombian city
events.summary: A car bomb detonated in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio on Monday, destroying a local governor's office and surrounding buildings, President Abelardo de la Espriella said. The right-wing leader has conducted a major crackdown on the country's drug trade, in response to left-wing FARC rebels who have stepped up attacks over the past two years. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.

events.title: Russian losses on Ukrainian front top 700,000 including missing
events.summary: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties, including soldiers missing on the frontline, after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland explains.
